An..Ch, 1339. Idem Carotas hospitibus de Rosenberga ti bertates Lipcstnsiiim largitur.

CLXXXVI. Nos Carolus, D. Gr. Rex Hung. etc. Memo riae commendamus tenore praesentium, quibus ex- pedit vniuersis, quod Hanus villicus, Petrus di et us de Scepusi. Kunchul, ciues de Rosenberg pro se et pro vniueisis ciuibus et hospitibus ipsorum, nos trae Maiestatis accedendo praesentium, petie- runt nos humillime, et denote supplicando, flagi- tando, quatenus eisdem libertates populorum, seu hospitum nostrorum de Lipche, in terra Liptouien. existent, annuentes, de regiae benignitatis clementia dare et concedere dignaremur. Jgitur nos, cum ex officio suseepti regiminis, iustis petentium desideriis aures exaudibiles praebere debeamus, regio cum fa- uore oecurrentes, considerantes ex ipsis libertatibus numerositatem populorum dietae possessionis nostrae de Rosenberg augmentatam, eteandembabitatoribus dilatan, intuitu fidelitatum eorum, voto et sup plicationi ipsorum satisfacere, et respondere para- ti, nostrae incumbit Maiestati, cum debito effectu 577 cupientes, has eidem infrascriptas libertates, de gratia pietatis regiae, ad mod um. libertatum prae- dictorum hospitum nostrorum de Lipche duximus concedendas: vt villicum seu iudicem more hospi tum nostrorum de dicta Lipche inter se eligereva- leant, quem de communi volunt voluntate, qui omnes causas inter se emergentes iudicabit , postquam a nobis legitime fuerit confirmatus. Item concessi- mus, quod ab omni Iudicum , Baronum, et specia- litercomitis deLiptou iudicio, descensu penitus sint exempti ; et quod nullus super ipsos descensum prae- sumat facere violentum- Praeterea aquam Revu- cze , piscationi congruentem, reliquimus eisdemho- spitibus piscandi. Concessimus etiam, vt iidem ho- spites nostri intra metas eorum infrascriptas, abs que praeiudicio iuris alieni, vbique locorum venan- di, aues capiendi, piscandi et molendina constru- endi liberam habeant facultatem. Item concessi mus, vt de syluis nostris, et aquis liberam habe ant facultatem quaerendi mineras aun , argenti et cupri, vbicunque poterit inueniri ; de quibus, cum inuenire poterint, nobis seruient secundum quod de a liis auri fodinis, et argenti fodinis regiae con- sueuerunt impendere Maiestati. Praeterea, vt in eadem terra nostra facilius valeant commorari, ipsorum numero augmentato, gaudendo certa lege, ordinauimus, vt singulis annis iidem nobis 50 mar cas in tribus terminis infrascriptis nobis soluere teneantur. Ita quod in festo B. Georgy Marty ris XX. marcas, item in festo Beati Michaelis Arch- angeli X. marcas, et XX. in Natiuitate Domini. Item, quod volumus, terram et omnia alia iura, quae intra metas ipsorum continentur , certis me tis limitata possidere valeant perpetuo et habere. 578 In his autem omnibus lihertatibus per nos conces~ sis more dictorum hospitum nostrornm de Lipche eosdem volumus gratulan*. Metae autem dictorum hospitum nostrorum de Rosemberg, vt ex relatio ne Magistri Thomae, filii Petri Castellani de Cho- kakeö et Comitis Liptouiensis intelleximus, hoc modo distinguuntur. entries.english:
1339. The same King Carolus grants the inhabitants of Rosenberg the liberties of the inhabitants of Lipche.

CLXXXVI. We, Carolus, by the grace of God King of Hungary, etc., commit to memory by these presents, which are useful to all, that Hanus, the reeve, and Petrus called de Scepusi, Kunchul, citizens of Rosenberg, appeared before our Majesty on behalf of themselves and all their fellow citizens and inhabitants, and humbly and devoutly petitioned us to graciously grant them the liberties of our people, or inhabitants, of Lipche in the land of Liptov. Therefore, since it is our duty in undertaking governance to give a hearing to the just requests of petitioners, and since we graciously consider that these liberties would increase the population of the aforesaid possession of ours, Rosenberg, and extend its settlement, in view of their loyalty, it is incumbent upon our Majesty to satisfy and respond to their wish and petition with due effect. Accordingly, by royal favor and grace, we have decided to grant them the liberties set out below, after the manner of the aforesaid inhabitants of Lipche: that they may elect from among themselves a reeve or judge, as do our aforesaid inhabitants of Lipche, whom they choose by common consent, and who shall judge all cases arising among them after he has been duly confirmed by us. We have also granted that they shall be entirely exempt from the jurisdiction and lodging obligations of all judges and barons, especially the Count of Liptov, and that no one shall presume to impose a forcible lodging upon them. We have also left them the Revúca stream, suitable for fishing, so that those inhabitants may fish there. We have further granted that within the boundaries set out below, without prejudice to another’s rights, they may freely hunt, catch birds, fish, and build mills wherever they wish. They shall also have the free right to prospect in our forests and waters for gold, silver, and copper mines wherever these may be found; when they find them, they shall render to us what is customarily owed to our royal Majesty from other gold and silver mines. Moreover, so that they may more easily remain in this land of ours and increase their numbers while enjoying a defined law, we have decreed that each year they shall pay us fifty marks in the following three installments: twenty marks on the feast of St George the Martyr, ten marks on the feast of St Michael the Archangel, and twenty at the Nativity of the Lord. We further will that they may hold and possess in perpetuity the land and all other rights contained within their boundaries, marked by fixed limits. In all these liberties granted by us, we wish them to enjoy the same customs as the aforesaid inhabitants of Lipche. The boundaries of our aforesaid inhabitants of Rosenberg, as we have learned from the report of Master Thomas, son of Petrus, castellan of Chokakeö and Count of Liptov, are distinguished as follows: the first boundary begins, etc. Given at Lipche, in the province of Zvolen, on the Tuesday after the feast of St Martin the Confessor. In the year of the Lord 1390 (40).

This letter is copied in the form of a privilege. It was written in 1340; therefore the date is erroneously read as 1390, and it should instead be assigned either to 1339 or 1340. Transcribed from the Thurocz archive by God. Keler. Anal. Tom. IV, p. 497.
